answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Every claim climbs the spiral of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the summit re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the pearl of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on economic security through validator rotation. Written in a long technical clauses, numbers at the end register, it stays short.
